headline: Fox Mandal & Associates advises landowners on revenue-sharing joint development with Puravankara in East Bengaluru
sum: Fox Mandal & Associates acted as counsel to landowners in structuring and negotiating a revenue-sharing joint development agreement (JDA) with Puravankara Limited for a multi-acre residential apartment project in East Bengaluru. The transaction is representative of capital-efficient real estate partnering in one of India's fastest-growing residential markets.
implication: Revenue-sharing JDAs are a capital-efficient partnership model increasingly favoured in Bengaluru's residential development; counsel must carefully structure landowner return mechanisms and exit clauses to protect both developer scale and owner yield expectations.
detail: Fox Mandal & Associates advised on the structuring, negotiation and documentation of a revenue-sharing joint development transaction between landowners and Puravankara Limited for a residential apartment project in East Bengaluru. The transaction structure involved a JDA rather than outright land sale, reflecting market preference for capital-light acquisition methods. Puravankara announced multiple such transactions in East Bengaluru's emerging micro-markets (Balagere, Mandur-Budigere, Sarjapur) through 2025–26, all structured under JDA frameworks with estimated GDVs ranging from ₹1,000–₹2,300 crore.

framework.ref: Real Estate (Regulation) Development and Management Act, 2016 (RERA)
framework.note: Central; RERA compliance mandatory for any residential project above ₹100 cr GDV; registration of JDA and disclosure of project cost & schedule.
Central; governs the creation, transfer and enforcement of interests in land; material to JDA enforceability as a contract for sale.
Central; legitimacy, consideration and performance of JDA terms; indemnity and liability clauses.
Central (if property in Karnataka); JDA instruments must be properly stamped; ad valorem duty typically on market value of land.
Central; optional registration of JDA strengthens title and creates presumption; registration guidelines vary by state.
State; land classification, conversion consent, and revenue record updates may be required before development.

framework.ref: Karnataka Municipalities Act, 1964 / Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961
framework.note: State; planning approval, site plan clearance, and building permission prerequisite to development commencement.
Central; capital gains treatment of land transfer by landowner; cost of acquisition and indexation relief on revenue distribution.

framework.ref: Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (Sections 7, 8, Schedule II)
framework.note: Central; GST @ 5% on services rendered by developer; exemption on transfer of land itself; JDA classification for GST purposes critical.

conditions: Revenue-sharing arrangement between developer and landowners (specific split ratio not disclosed)
Regulatory approval from Bengaluru Municipal Corporation / BBMP
Completion of title verification and land encumbrance clearance
Financing arrangement by Puravankara (if not all-cash development)
approvals: Stamp duty assessment and registration (optional but recommended)
structure.novel: Revenue-sharing JDA structure (not outright land sale or fixed land cost buyout); landowner retains upside participation in project economics rather than fixed exit. This capital-light model is increasingly adopted by tier-1 developers to acquire land in high-demand zones without upfront capex commitment.

triggers.note: Mandatory for any residential project above ₹100 cr; JDA must be registered with RERA Authority; breach of registration attracts penal interest and prosecution.
Site plan approval and building permit prerequisite; zoning, density and use classification for residential on the specific land parcel.
JDA document must be stamped ad valorem on deemed consideration (market value of land); under-stamping can render document inadmissible.
Characterization of transaction (goods vs. service vs. supply of land) determines tax incidence; JDA services taxable @ 5%, land transfer exempt.
